sections.title: Reserving a locker at the swimming pool

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: I can book a long-term locker for you at the pool. It will stay assigned to you between sessions, unlike the small lockers by the showers.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: All right. Let’s go through the details.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: What have you put down for the booking surname?

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: I have put Reed on the record. That is the spelling with two Es.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: What should I write for the locker size?

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: The medium size will fit your bag. All the large lockers are taken this week.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: And what is the locker number?

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: Your locker number is 28. The row starts beside the lift and continues towards the showers.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: Could you confirm the collection day?

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: The key will be ready on Wednesday. We do not issue new keys during the Tuesday cleaning session.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: What have you put down for the collection desk?

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: Collect the key from reception. The small kiosk by the pool only sells refreshments.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: What should I write for the refundable deposit?

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: The deposit is twelve pounds. We return it when you bring back the key in working condition.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: And what is the card colour?

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: We will give you an orange card. It identifies this type of locker rather than a swimming lesson.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: Could you confirm the renewal month?

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: The booking can be renewed in August. You will receive a reminder near the end of July.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: What have you put down for the item prohibited in locker?

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: Do not leave food inside. We have had trouble keeping the lockers clean when items are left overnight.

script.speaker: Swimmer
script.text: What should I write for the key returned in an?

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: Return the key in an envelope with the locker number written on the outside.

script.speaker: Attendant
script.text: Keep the reference until you receive the key. The new lockers are clearly marked, but ask at the desk if you cannot find yours.

sections.title: A short route through the bicycle park

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: The site plan shows our junction in the centre, with north at the top. This park is for practising slow, controlled movement, so walk between the stations.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: The balance lane is east of the junction, along the path to the right. It is marked by a low white line.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: The brake slope is north of the junction. It is the short ramp shown at the top.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: The helmet stand is west of the junction, on the left. You can collect the equipment before walking to the next station.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: The rest shelter is south of the junction, towards the bottom of the plan. Please leave the entrance clear.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: The safety briefing lasts seven minutes. We will practise stopping after everyone has heard it.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: I will set out cones along the practice boundary. Stay within that line when you are on a bicycle.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: Use the lowest gear for the first run. We are practising balance and will not ask you to ride fast.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: After use, put borrowed helmets on the shelf. A volunteer checks them before they go back on the stand.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: When you hear the whistle, finish the movement and stop. It is the signal to end practice.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: The drinking tap is beside the fence. Use it before you return to the street.

script.speaker: Trainer
script.text: The session ends here. Bring borrowed equipment back before leaving, even if you plan to return later in the day.

sections.title: Understanding the sound of a loose part

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: A loose part can make a sound when a structure is shaken. We will use a simple model to distinguish a repeated contact from sound caused by the material vibrating as a whole.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Our model is a wooden box with a loose piece inside. The lid stays closed during the first comparison.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: When the box is tilted this way, the piece first strikes the left wall. You can hear that contact after the movement starts.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: A thin pad against the wall can reduce the contact sound. We will add it without changing the shape of the box.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Try to keep the speed of movement the same. Shaking faster would affect the strength of the contact.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Mark the microphone position on the floor. If it moves closer, a change in loudness could be misleading.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: In the second comparison, hold the piece in place. This helps us check which sounds are still present without the repeated contact.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Record how many separate contacts you hear during each shake. Counting the contacts is different from rating their loudness.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Play both recordings at the same volume. Changing it between them would make a loudness comparison unreliable.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Switch off the background fan if possible. It can cover the quieter contact sounds in the recording.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Keep a note of how the box was supported. Holding it against the bench can change which parts vibrate.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: When you write up the test, say exactly what changed. A sound by itself is rarely enough to diagnose the condition of a real object.
